title: Finiteness descends under fpqc base change
statement: For scheme morphisms f:X→S and g:T→S [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], suppose g is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and quasi-compact (the inverse image of every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact). If X×_S T→T [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], then f is finite.

proof.text: Invoke the already proved source-library declaration AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.descendsAlong_surjective_inf_flat_inf_quasicompact (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FlatDescent, lines 106–111). DescendsAlong is exactly the assertion for a cartesian square; apply its of_isPullback field to the base-change square. No new proof obligation or module is introduced.
